what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/drive-the-screen: look at, find on, drive, and list the actions for the person's Mac screen, as computer runs of read-data/drive-the-screen.mjs.

payload.label: See what is on the person's computer screen
payload.job: Read the person's computer screen: the app in front (or one named), its controls from the accessibility tree and the text on its windows from the pixels, with where each is
payload.description: Returns the app, the displays, and the things on the screen (role, label, centre and size, and the actions each offers) in points from the top left of the main display, never coordinates guessed from a picture. Text from the pixels is kept to the app's own windows. Read-only. Uses this Mac's existing Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions. The person can turn on an optional grant policy in their screen-driving settings folder; calls cannot change that policy.

app.description: The running app to read (its name or bundle id); the app in front when left out.

sources.description: Where to read from: ax (the accessibility tree) and/or ocr (the pixels read as text).

settings_folder.description: The folder the person keeps their screen-driving settings in (the one holding .trillion/screen-driving: grants, rules, places), granted to this tool as change-a-folder. Left out, the run starts from an empty folder, so only the shipped rules apply.

payload.description: Describe the target by what it is called or what kind it is, never by coordinates. Returns the ranked matches with where each is now. Read-only. Uses this Mac's existing Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions. The person can turn on an optional grant policy in their screen-driving settings folder; calls cannot change that policy.

payload.label: Operate the person's computer screen
payload.job: Click, press, type, scroll, drag or use keys on the person's computer, finding the target by what it is called and checking afterwards what really changed
payload.description: One call looks at the screen, finds the target, does the action, looks again and says what changed. action is one the computer keeps (tool:screen-actions lists them; new ones are added as data on the computer). Give expect, a list of { target, min?, max? } or { changed }, and verified says whether the screen shows it; without expect, verified is null and the change seen is reported. dry_run shows the steps without doing them. Press and set_value act through the accessibility tree and do not move the person's pointer; click, type and key do. A target that moved or vanished is refused, never guessed. Uses this Mac's existing Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions. The person can turn on an optional grant policy in their screen-driving settings folder; calls cannot change that policy.

payload.label: Click on this Mac's screen
payload.job: Do one thing in a named app on the person's Mac: bring it to the front, click a thing found by its accessibility label or role (or a point from a fresh look), type text or press a key, with a screen capture identity before and after. Never in System Settings' Privacy & Security, a password field, a payment confirmation or the Mac's authentication sheets.
payload.description: Runs on the person's own Mac under the app that runs tools there, with that app's own Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions (a run whose parent is not the app is refused). `action` is open (bring the named running app to the front), click (needs `target`), type (`text`, after clicking `target` when given) or press_key (`keys` such as cmd+s or return). `target` is a label, { match: { label | role | title | description | value | identifier | text } }, or { at: { x, y } } in global points from a fresh look, which resolves to the smallest element under the point. Each run observes the app, finds the target, judges it against a hard deny list, acts, observes again and says what changed; `captures` holds the BLAKE3 identity of a screen capture before and after. The deny list has no switch: a click, key or text in System Settings' Privacy & Security panes, into a password, passcode or passkey field, on a payment confirmation, or into the Mac's authentication sheets (SecurityAgent, coreautha) is refused before anything is done, a rehearsal (dry_run) too, and the refusal names its rule in `refused_by_rule`. Without the Mac permission it answers the permission it needs (`permission`: ax_trusted or screen_capture) and does nothing.

app.description: The running app, by its name or bundle id

target.description: A label, { match: { field: text } }, or { at: { x, y } } from a fresh look

keys.description: What press_key presses, such as cmd+s or return

expect.description: What must be on the screen after: { target, min?, max? } or { changed: true | false }, or a list of them

dry_run.description: Find and judge the target, do nothing

settings_folder.description: The folder that holds the person's screen-driving settings
